text: The painted pedestrian crossing has almost disappeared; drivers cannot make out its white stripes.
A broad section of carriageway has dropped noticeably, leaving the middle of the junction lower than its edges.
A raised bubble has formed in the road's asphalt coating and is lifting the surface into a dome.
The tactile paving tiles at the crossing have broken studs, so the guidance surface is incomplete.
A temporary steel road plate has lifted at one end, creating a hard step for passing cars.
The concrete pedestrian refuge in the middle of the road is chipped away and needs repair.
The bottle recycling bank is full to its opening, and more empty containers have been left around it.
An old television and a broken computer were abandoned beside the communal bins for removal.
Empty produce crates are strewn across the public market after the stalls closed.
White foam packing pieces are scattered over the public square following a delivery.
Sacks of unwanted clothing have been left on the municipal stair landing and need collection.
Refuse bags left for pickup have torn open, spilling their contents across the shared collection area.
The public streetlight shines with such harsh glare into our bedroom that we need its brightness checked.
Each time a car passes, its headlights trigger the streetlamp sensor and the pavement light switches off.
Rainwater is collecting inside the streetlight's transparent cover; droplets are visible around the bulb.
The mounting bracket holding the public lamp is badly corroded and needs inspection.
The lamp on the public footpath has changed from white to an unusual purple colour.
The base of the lighting column has loose bolts, and the pole wobbles slightly when touched; no wires are visible.
Piano scales from the next flat continue past midnight at a volume that keeps our child awake.
Our neighbour makes very loud phone calls beside the shared bedroom wall every night.
Someone jumps repeatedly on an exercise machine in the apartment above during sleeping hours.
Children run and stamp along the residential hallway very early each morning, disturbing the flats.
A person whistles sharply and repeatedly on the pavement beneath our windows long after midnight.
A late-night pavement game involves repeated ball bouncing directly outside our sleeping area.
